_what: How the letters in an ad are PHYSICALLY MADE — the material, surface and edge treatment of the letterforms. Not the typeface: a typeface is which shapes, a letterform is what they are built out of. The image teardown labels every text element with one of these ids and its own free phrase; stage 6 carries both into the type layer; stage 7 tells the generator how ours are made.
_why: the owner, 2026-09-25: "the nuance of the style of the creative is lost because a lot of these swipes have specific styles. Claymation-style text is going to look different than you just writing text on an image." Everything else about type was already recorded — class, width, weight, case, size, hex, tracking, leading. This was not, so every rebuild set flat digital type: right for a flat-digital swipe, wrong for every other kind.
_rule: A row that does not fit is never bent to fit. The teardown answers `none-fits` and proposes a NAMED row in one line, and the work carries on — same rule the format, style, framework and awareness lists already run (stage 2b). the owner signs a proposed row before it becomes real; until then it is a draft nobody is blocked by.

letterforms.name: Flat digital type
letterforms.what: Set type with no depth of any kind: solid fill, hard clean edge, no shadow, bevel, texture or outline. The most common answer and a real one — most direct-response statics are this.
letterforms.how_to_see_it: The letter edge is mathematically clean at full zoom and the fill is one unbroken colour. Nothing separates the letter from its ground except the colour change.

letterforms.name: Extruded 3D
letterforms.what: Letters pushed back into space with a visible side wall, usually bevelled at the front edge and casting a shadow onto what is behind them.
letterforms.how_to_see_it: A second colour runs down one side of every stroke — the extrusion — consistently to the same vanishing direction across all letters.

letterforms.name: Moulded clay
letterforms.what: Letters that read as modelled by hand out of a soft solid — claymation lettering. Rounded, slightly irregular, lit as a real object in the scene.
letterforms.how_to_see_it: Every stroke has its own soft highlight and contact shadow, thickness varies where a hand would have pressed, and no two identical letters are truly identical.

letterforms.name: Hand-lettered marker
letterforms.what: Written by hand with a marker, brush or pen on a real surface. Stroke weight follows pressure and speed, and the ends of strokes show the tool.
letterforms.how_to_see_it: Line weight changes within a single stroke, ends taper or blot, and the baseline wanders.

letterforms.name: Hand-drawn, textured fill
letterforms.what: Drawn letterforms whose fill carries a texture — hatching, stipple, grain, risograph — rather than a flat colour, often with a drawn shadow offset behind.
letterforms.how_to_see_it: The fill is not uniform at zoom: it is made of marks. A shadow, where present, is drawn rather than rendered.

letterforms.name: Cut paper
letterforms.what: Letters that read as cut or torn from sheet material and laid on the ground, lifting slightly off it.
letterforms.how_to_see_it: A thin hard shadow hugs one side of each letter, edges show a cut or torn quality, and the paper's own surface catches light differently from the ground.

letterforms.name: Embossed into the surface
letterforms.what: Letters pressed into or raised out of the material they sit on, carrying no colour of their own — they are the same material as the ground.
letterforms.how_to_see_it: The letters are legible only through highlight and shadow along their edges; sample the fill and it matches the background.

letterforms.name: Letterpress
letterforms.what: Printed with a physical impression: ink slightly heavier at the edge of each stroke, the paper visibly indented.
letterforms.how_to_see_it: Ink pools at stroke edges and thins in the middle, and the paper texture shows through the fill.

letterforms.name: Chrome
letterforms.what: Metallic letters with a bevelled edge reflecting an environment — a horizon line across the face of the letter is the tell.
letterforms.how_to_see_it: The fill is a gradient that inverts partway down every stroke, and the same reflection pattern repeats across all letters.

letterforms.name: Neon tube
letterforms.what: Letters as glowing tube, with light spilling onto the surface behind them.
letterforms.how_to_see_it: Stroke width is constant, the core is brighter than the edge, and the ground immediately around the letters is lit by them.

letterforms.name: Chalk or dust
letterforms.what: Letters drawn in a dry medium on a dark ground, edges dusty and broken rather than clean.
letterforms.how_to_see_it: Coverage is uneven within strokes, edges fade rather than stop, and the ground's texture breaks through.

letterforms.name: Knockout through a bar
letterforms.what: Letters cut out of a solid panel so the picture or ground shows through them, or the panel colour shows through the letters.
letterforms.how_to_see_it: A hard-edged rectangle of solid colour holds the line, and the letters are the absence of that colour rather than a colour of their own.

letterforms.name: Outlined social caption
letterforms.what: White (or bright) letters with a hard contrasting outline or drop shadow so they stay legible over any footage — the native look of social captions and memes.
letterforms.how_to_see_it: A uniform stroke of a second colour follows every letter's contour at constant width, regardless of what is behind it.

letterforms.name: Native system caption
letterforms.what: Type rendered by a device or app rather than designed — a screenshot's own UI text, a native story caption, a search bar, a comment.
letterforms.how_to_see_it: It sits in a platform's own chrome at the platform's own size, and the typeface is a system face rather than a chosen one.
